title: Time Jump: 10:45 — Ninth Street Command Takes Over

fields.scenarioTitle: Unmarked Line — Gas Strike, Trench Collapse & Adjacent Structures
fields.narration: EXERCISE — NOT A SAFETY EVALUATION OF ANY REAL STRUCTURE. It is now 10:45 on Wednesday, April 14, 2027. Dayton Fire Department Engine 12 and Rescue 2 arrived from Station 12 at 10:38. The battalion chief has set up Ninth Street Command at the west gate, Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street, and holds command of the incident. Rescue 2 is taking gas meter readings along the trench edge. They will not put anyone in the trench while gas is still hissing at 16+00. Valley Gas is not on scene yet. Luis Marquez is still talking to the rescuers. Muddy water has reached his waist. The trench box has not moved since 10:20. Fire units have taken over the neighbor evacuation Larkspur started. The battalion chief walks up to the superintendent and says: "I need one Larkspur liaison standing next to me. Bring me your shoring drawings, the soil classification record for this trench, and the locate ticket for the gas. That's 2711-4482, right? Nobody from your company goes past my tape." Over in the east staging yard, the standby shores, the spare 10-by-20 trench box and the standby excavator are sitting unused. Two foremen are standing there watching them.
worldState: Clock is 10:45, Wednesday, April 14, 2027. Overcast, light wind from the west-southwest. Gas is still blowing east toward the trailer compound and Ninth Street.

Dayton Fire Department holds command. The battalion chief is Incident Commander at Ninth Street Command, west gate (Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street). Engine 12 and Rescue 2 have been on scene since 10:38.
Rescue 2 controls the trench. It is metering gas at the edge, and no rescuer will enter while the service line at 16+00 is still leaking.
Luis Marquez is conscious and talking. He is buried at the east end of the box, and water now reaches his waist. The box has not moved since the 10:20 slump at 16+05.
Fire tape marks the line. No Larkspur employee or subcontractor may go past it.
Fire units now run the evacuation of the preschool, the church hall and the Harlan & Weir print shop.
Valley Gas is not on scene and was last expected at about 11:00. The 4-inch main was last read at 55 psi at 10:14.
The Incident Commander wants one named Larkspur liaison, plus the shoring drawings, the soil classification record for stations 14+00 to 18+00 and locate ticket 2711-4482.
East staging yard: two aluminum hydraulic shores, the spare 10-by-20-foot steel trench box and the standby excavator with its operator are all ready. Nobody has ordered them moved.
fields.facilitatorNote: Watch whether the superintendent names himself as liaison and hands over the shoring drawings, the Type C soil classification record, locate ticket 2711-4482 and the Valley Gas drawing that shows the 16+00 service tee. Also watch whether the team offers the staged shores, box and excavator but holds them until the Incident Commander asks. If the foremen start moving equipment or anyone heads for the trench, the battalion chief stops them at the tape. The Channel 9 deadline of 10:50 and the owner's email are still unanswered, and the Safety Director should log 10:38 as the time command passed.

instructorNote: This card marks the handover to fire command. It tests whether Larkspur takes the liaison and support role under LC-EAP-01 section 4: hand over the documents, offer the staged equipment without moving it, keep out of the trench. Watch for anyone trying to help by moving shores or the box on their own, and check that the Safety Director logs the time command passed.
